committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal contracting personnel, DHS/FEMA administrators, and entities engaging in emergency disaster response contracting.
dimensions.evidence: contract entered into or extended by the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency

dimensions.assessment: Lengthens the timeframe allowed for noncompetitive urgent disaster contracts and adds ongoing reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: extends the maximum duration of noncompetitive Department of Homeland Security (DHS) contracts for disaster response and recovery from 150 days to one year

dimensions.assessment: Involves federal disaster procurement funds and requires reporting on taxpayer savings and amounts obligated.
dimensions.evidence: amounts obligated by the Administrator for each contract

dimensions.assessment: Repeals an obsolete contracting restriction under the Post-Katrina Emergency Management Reform Act of 2006 and institutes new annual reporting mandates.
dimensions.evidence: amend the Post-Katrina Management Reform Act of 2006 to repeal certain obsolete requirements

dimensions.assessment: Permanently alters procurement rules, paired with a 5-year annual reporting requirement.
dimensions.evidence: annually thereafter until the date that is 5 years thereafter

missing_information: Historical dollar volume of noncompetitive contracts that previously hit the 150-day limit.
importance_detail.rationale: Extends the maximum duration for noncompetitive DHS disaster response contracts from 150 days to one year and mandates 5 years of annual congressional reports.
